answer: Names are rationed by who may grant them. Each identity stands on one pearl, a grant drawn from a small standing set of authorities, each releasing a fixed quota per epoch and publishing every recipient it has already blessed. A grant is worthless unless a cipher older than the epoch countersigns it, and reconciliation across authorities lays bare any cluster issued in one burst. A farm wanting k names must work a pool that thins as it consumes it, paying bribes to ever scarcer signers, while a forge that mints ungranted keys buys nothing at all.
